description: Create core/examples.py with few-shot LinkedIn post examples and rebuild core/voice.py with a shorter, punchier voice system that produces human-sounding output
steps: Create core/examples.py as a new module with 5-6 high-quality few-shot LinkedIn post examples demonstrating different writing styles: (1) Nigerian professional storytelling - warm, communal, specific numbers, (2) Mid-scene opener - drops you into a moment before context, (3) Withhold-the-lesson - tells what happened, lets reader figure out the takeaway, (4) Communal/warm style - uses 'we' framing, direct about results, (5) Data-driven but human - numbers forward with personality, (6) Ambiguous ending with no CTA. Each example should be 150-400 words, feel genuinely human-written, and demonstrate the exact quality the app should produce. Include a get_examples(n=3) function that returns a random subset.

Rewrite HUMAN_VOICE_PRIMER in core/voice.py - reduce from ~600 words to ~250 words. Make it a creative brief, not a rulebook. Bake Nigerian warmth (communal framing, 'we' not just 'I', directness about money/results, comfort with longer flowing sentences) into the core voice natively rather than as an addon. Keep the core principles: specificity over polish, earned honesty, real rhythm.

Consolidate BANNED in core/voice.py - keep the same banned phrases but remove the verbose category headers and explanations. Group tighter. The list itself is fine, just make the formatting leaner so it takes fewer tokens.

Rewrite HUMAN_SIGNATURES in core/voice.py - make it less prescriptive. Instead of numbered rules with explanations, show brief examples. Keep the same 8 categories (specific numbers, time anchors, places, dialogue, self-interruption, contrast, vulnerability, industry proof) but present them as demonstrations rather than instructions.

Rebuild STRUCTURE_RULES in core/voice.py with these key changes: (a) KILL the rigid 'one idea per line' rule - replace with 'vary paragraph length: mix single lines with 2-3 sentence paragraphs like a real writer', (b) LOOSEN hook length from 'under 12 words ideally, 15 max' to 'under 25 words, specificity matters more than brevity', (c) ALLOW hooks that open mid-scene (not just claims), (d) REMOVE 'no questions as hooks' rule - allow specific questions, (e) Add a 'no CTA' option acknowledging best posts sometimes just end, (f) Add structural variety instruction: pick different paragraph structures each time.
Update voice_block() and short_voice_block() functions if their signatures change. Keep backward compatibility - they should still return strings usable in prompts.

Ensure the BANNED constant still contains all the same quoted phrases (core/validator.py at import time extracts them via regex on quoted strings). Do NOT remove any phrase from inside quotes - only restructure the surrounding text.
acceptance_criteria: core/examples.py exists with get_examples() returning list of example post strings
HUMAN_VOICE_PRIMER is under 300 words (count via len(HUMAN_VOICE_PRIMER.split()))
All previously banned phrases still appear quoted in BANNED (validator.py regex extraction still works)
STRUCTURE_RULES no longer contains 'one idea per line' or 'Under 12 words'
STRUCTURE_RULES allows questions as hooks and no-CTA endings
voice_block() still returns a string containing all four sections
Nigerian warmth/communal framing is in the core HUMAN_VOICE_PRIMER, not a separate section
verification: Run pytest tests/ -ra --tb=short - all tests must pass (test_voice.py will need updating since structure rules changed)
Run python -c "from core.voice import HUMAN_VOICE_PRIMER; print(len(HUMAN_VOICE_PRIMER.split()))" and confirm under 300
Run python -c "from core.examples import get_examples; print(len(get_examples(3)))" and confirm it returns 3 examples
